concerns: The proposed distinction is misleading for the exact side-to-side sense: Malaysian Malay ordinarily uses lebar too.
response.cue_rationale: The narrowed sense “having a large side-to-side extent” favors lebar in both varieties; Malaysian luas does not reliably express this exact physical-width sense.
material_concerns: The pair presents luas as the Malaysian counterpart of Indonesian lebar, but luas more typically means broad/extensive or large in area; lebar is the ordinary exact term for physical width in both varieties.

preference_risk.rationale: Lebar is plausibly ordinary in both Indonesian and Malaysian Malay for physical side-to-side width, so the proposed lebar/luas preference is not dependable.

response.rationale: Both forms can translate broad English uses of “wide,” but they do not reliably represent the same precise sense. For side-to-side extent, lebar is ordinary in both Indonesian and Malaysian Malay.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: The shared form lebar is ordinary for this exact sense in both countries, defeating the proposed national preference for luas.
